articleTitle: Terahertz Imaging Through Dust
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate that THz imaging can provide virtually unimpaired visibility through a dense dust environment that would otherwise result in zero visibility under conventional optical imaging. This work highlights a technological solution to a long-standing problem experienced by conventional optical imaging in brownout conditions.

articleTitle: Enhancing the MEMS Gyroscope Physical Assurance Using Quantum Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum sensing techniques to bolster the security of MEMS gyroscopes against acoustic attacks. By harnessing quantum sensing's precision and immunity, we introduce an innovative strategy to protect MEMS-based systems, ensuring their reliability amid evolving security challenges.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning Control of an Avatar and Exoskeleton
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We present a novel approach for controlling a unilateral lower extremity exoskeleton with deep reinforcement learning utilizing a Long-term Short-term Memory network with a Proximal Policy Optimization Model. We create an avatar in Unity to reflect the movement while also controlling our exoskeleton.

articleTitle: Improvements in Target Detection Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: A new approach using computer vision/machine learning (ML) algorithms to improve thermal target detection performance is discussed. ERDC's prototype two-step environment informed automatic target detection and recognition (ATD/R) algorithm shows a greater than 50% improvement in sub-surface target detection as compared to other ML ATD/R algorithms.

articleTitle: pW IR Sensing with MEMS coupled to Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: This paper focuses on infrared (IR) sensors based on merging radiofrequency (RF) aluminum nitride (AIN) contour mode resonators (CMRs) integrated with spectrally-selective IR metasurfaces. Thousands of this type of innovative sensors were fabricated and characterize using a dedicated automatized approach. The proposed system utilizes a microprobe to sequentially test and characterize thousands of devices on a wafer, employing optical and RF interrogation techniques, dedicating ~20 s to each device. Analysis of the collected data provides insights into sensor response relative to design parameters and geometrical variations. Additionally, new interrogation systems are proposed to enhance the sensing performance of the sensors. The devices were able to detect weak IR signals with < 100 pW of power and exhibit a noise equivalent power (NEP) in the fW/sqrt(Hz) range at room temperature. These metrics highlight their potential of this technology in a wide range of applications, including spectroscopy, imaging, and security, among others.

articleTitle: A Modular Electromagnetic Model Framework: Concept and Example
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Modeling and simulation of defense relevant electromagnetic phenomena often requires expansive tools with high licensing costs and a steep learning curve. A framework for an open-source modular tool is defined, with an example provided of a module describing nanostructured optical limiters.

articleTitle: Advancing PCB Assurance Towards Netlist Extraction with the Integration of X-Ray Imaging and Semi-Supervised Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: PCBs are indispensable components that enable the functionality of modern electronics across numerous industries. This study presents a framework for their semi-supervised netlist extraction by addressing the challenges during X-ray tomography. Leveraging AI models during annotation saves time while allowing SMEs to fix AI-generated errors.

articleTitle: Nested Anti-Resonant Hollow-Core Fiber for Low-Loss Multi-Mode Guidance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We present a multi-mode nested anti-resonant hollow-core fiber optimized for 1550 nm operation. This fiber achieves exceptional low-loss transmission and supports multi-mode guidance with propagation losses as low as 0.06 dB/m. Characterization reveals a wide bandwidth transmission window exceeding 250 nm, with loss <0.1 dB/m.

articleTitle: Manipulating Self-Collimation to Guide and Multiplex Light Using Photonic Crystals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Spatial variation can be introduced to photonic crystal lattices to control the direction and phase of propagating light. This work investigates the limits of this spatial variation and introduces photonic crystal structures for light-guiding applications through modeling, simulation, fabrication, and testing.

articleTitle: Data-driven reduced order models for radar imaging in multi-scattering environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Conventional imaging algorithms for solving the inverse wave problem can be polluted by multiple echoes and other artifacts. We developed an approach, called the Lippmann-Schwinger-Lanczos algorithm, which “absorbs” much of the non-linearity of the classical approach to inverse scattering, thus making the subsequent imaging a lot more straightforward.

articleTitle: Nanostructured Films for Advancing Meta-Optics and Surface Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We analyze thin films, metastructures, and surfaces with multipolar coupling and bound states in the continuum, leading to strong and narrow resonances. We show that we can control the nanostructure parameters and enable directional scattering from the metastructure. Improved quality of the thin film results in enhanced electronic and photonic functionalities.

articleTitle: Tunable long-wave infrared filters based on a dense array of resonance cavities and phase-change materials
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We present polarization and angle insensitive tunable, long-wave infrared filters based on a dense array of phase change resonators. Patterning arrays with different heights and diameters readily tune the baseline resonant wavelength and linewidth of the spectral response, while annealing the PCM at different temperatures can further tune the resonant wavelength.

articleTitle: Cloud-Edge Framework for Multi-Vehicle Deployment Control using Spiking Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Recent advances have spotlighted the use of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) for defense and surveillance, focusing on cooperative monitoring and exploration. However, these UAV systems face significant operational challenges due to limited computational and energy resources, affecting their endurance and effectiveness in critical missions. This study proposes a novel approach using Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) to overcome these limitations. SNNs, inspired by the human brain's processing efficiency, offer a shift towards more autonomous and adaptive UAV systems. Leveraging SNNs, we introduce a cloud-edge computational framework aimed at optimizing barrier coverage control and enhancing UAVs' monitoring capabilities within resource constraints. This SNN-based framework marks a considerable advancement in UAV operational capabilities, enabling longer missions, better area coverage, and adaptability to environmental changes. The effectiveness in achieving optimal barrier coverage sets a new benchmark for multivehicle systems in defense applications, underscoring the potential of brain-inspired computing in military operations and paving the way for future research in autonomous defense technologies.

articleTitle: Control of Light in Three Dimensions Using Spatially Variant Photonic Crystals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: This work demonstrates the ability of spatially variant photonic crystals to control the propagation of light in three dimensions. We explore the design, numerical analysis, and laboratory demonstration of these devices for unique light-guiding applications in the near-infrared spectrum.

articleTitle: Optical Signal Transport on Aerospace Platforms: ADC-Defined Limits on Digital Link Implementation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Photonic interconnects play a critical role in aerospace and defense RF platforms. This paper identifies ADC-imposed limitations on digital photonic interconnects, where analog-based solutions will continue to find demand.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Infrared Detection in Defense Applications: A Nanophotonic Approach Leveraging 2D Materials for Enhanced Mid-IR Absorption
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: In the domain of defense applications, infrared (IR) detection serves as a critical asset, underpinning technologies from advanced night vision and precision-guided military missile tracking to surveillance and reconnaissance systems. The quest for heightened accuracy and performance of these devices forms the crux of our research. This paper divulges a cutting-edge approach to the fabrication of the active layers in IR sensors and detectors, targeting the zenith of IR radiation absorption and detection efficacy. We introduce a nanophotonic multilayer absorber tailored for mid-infrared (mid-IR) wave absorption, capitalizing on the unique properties of 2D materials. Utilizing advanced inverse design algorithms inspired by evolutionary processes, we construct nanoscale structures composed of seven alternating layers. These layers are meticulously engineered to achieve perfect absorption in the critical 3–5 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> spectral range, all within a sub-micrometer thickness profile with an accuracy of 0.2 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>. This innovative design not only meets but exceeds the stringent size, weight, and power (SWaP) constraints, pivotal for deployment in next-generation defense systems, thereby substantially enhancing detection accuracy and operational readiness.

articleTitle: Development of High power UVC LED Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Improvements in UVC LED reliability, light extraction and wall plug efficiency rely on advancements in everything from epitaxial growth to device design. These innovations have enabled commercial devices to outperform legacy lamp technology in some disinfection applications—expanding the market growth for this technology

articleTitle: Plasmonic biosensors for real-time monitoring of harmful pathogens and biomolecules
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: This study focuses on a bottom-up approach for immobilizing gold nanorods (AuNRs) on glass substrates. These substrates were utilized to develop an optical immunosensor and a gene-sensor. Integration with microfluidic circuits enhances portability, highlighting potential point-of-care applications in challenging environments.

articleTitle: Intercalated Graphene and Colloidal Quantum Dots as a novel Architecture for UV/ Vis/NIR Multispectral Photodetection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We present a compact hybrid architecture of intercalated graphene and PbS quantum dots with independent electrical contacts for each graphene layer that allowing for detection of different spectral bands for each graphene layer without diffractive or splitting elements, showing a red shift toward the deeper layers.

articleTitle: Inhibited-Coupled Multi-Mode Hollow-Core Anti-Resonant Fibers for High Power Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We report a hollow-core anti-resonant fiber based on a strong-inhibited coupling, designed for high-power applications at 1064 nm. The fiber can support >45 spatial-modes with a loss of<100 dB/km and low-bend loss.

articleTitle: Human task performance on detecting distant targets under cluttered background in NIR and LWIR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: This study investigates human ability to detect distant targets in cluttered backgrounds using NIR and LWIR, aiming to facilitate AI performance analysis. Through perception tests and employing NV-IPM, it reveals key insights into how image quality influences detectability across NIR and LWIR scenarios.

articleTitle: Low Size, Weight, and Power Frequency Comb Modules for Deployed Optical Clocks, Radar Systems, and Quantum Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Performance levels, increased levels of system integration, and examples of fielded demonstrations of low size, weight, and power optical frequency combs will be discussed for potential next-generation deployed optical clocks, radar systems, and quantum applications.

articleTitle: Wide-Field-of-View Multi-Wavelength Metalens
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We illustrate how a stack of mutually transparent nonlocal metasurfaces can be used to realize an ultrathin multiwavelength lens stack for wide field of view (FoV) applications.

articleTitle: Time-varying Microwave Photonic Filter over 46-GHz Bandwidth with High Tuning Speed
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Time-varying (TV) filters, with the ability to precisely process non-stationary high-speed microwave signals, are fundamental building blocks in wireless communications, Radar/Lidar systems, advanced metrology, etc. [1]–[3]. To date, it remains challenging to achieve time-varying microwave filters with fully reconfigurable spectral transfer functions, large tuning bandwidth (>10GHz), and high tuning speed (into the GHz range) simultaneously. This set of specifications are particularly interesting for applications in 5G/6G and cognitive communications. For example, digital TV filters can achieve hyperfine frequency resolution and high reconfigurability; however, their real-time processing bandwidth is inherently limited to below a few hundreds of MHz [4], [5]. Recently, significant efforts have been devoted to the development of TV microwave filters through the microwave photonics (MWP) approach, so-called MWP filters (MWPFs), as these have been shown to enable broad operation bandwidth, fast tuning speed and an important degree of flexibility. However, current TV MPFs still fall short of the set of specifications defined above, being particularly limited in regards to their versatility and tuning speed [6], [7]. For example, a notable level of reconfigurability can be achieved by cascading an optical frequency comb source and a programmable optical filter, but the reconfiguration speed is still limited by the tuning speed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\sim$</tex> kHz) of the programmable optical filter [6]. On the other hand, a tuning speed of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 1$</tex> GHz has been demonstrated using other approaches, but in these solutions the degree of reconfigurability is still fairly limited [7].

articleTitle: Progress Toward Production Grade Infrared LED Scene Projector Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: this paper describes progress being made toward production grade infrared LED projectors.

articleTitle: Multiband strain balanced superlattice material system for third generation infrared detectors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Recent increasing interest in strain balanced Type-II superlattices material causing close attention from industry. Tremendous investment was drawn toward establishing strain balanced superlattice (SLS) as new alternative for infrared photodetectors across the broad range of infrared spectrum. In recent years, SLS material system has shown capability in particular specifications to compete with mature and standard mercury cadmium telluride for mid-wavelength and long-wavelength infrared detection. It has been great interest in SLS material system for applications aligned with the standard of third generation of infrared detectors. In this presentation, some recent progress in three color infrared photodetectors based on SLS material system will be presented.

articleTitle: Exploiting Quasi-Optics and Near-Field Trajectory Engineering for THz Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Millimeter and THz bands promise unprecedented data rates in future wireless systems. Here, we exploit near-field quasi-optics to realize beams that have no equivalent in the far-field and at lower frequencies. We show that curved self-accelerating beams offer opportunities for obstacle evasion, interference minimization, and physical layer security.

articleTitle: Controlling Light With Optical Metasurfaces and Chiral Liquid Crystals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Optical metasurfaces combined with chiral liquid crystals enable a new generation of optical components that integrate a light-tunable mirror and a controllable perfect absorber. This combination heralds a new era in optical technology, offering enhanced versatility and performance in manipulating light.

articleTitle: Silicon Photonics Under Siege: Unveiling Security Vulnerabilities Against SAW
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: The paper investigates challenges posed by acoustic wave interference on silicon photonic devices, explicitly focusing on MEMS and LiDAR systems. This study explores the impacts of ultrasound interference, offering insights into vulnerabilities and informing the development of countermeasures for ensuring the security of devices.

articleTitle: Characterization of Hot-carrier Enhanced Pixels for Out-of-band CMOS Camera
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We present optoelectronic characterization of ntype silicon pixels with a suite of plasmonic designs intended to generate and detect electron-hole pairs from incident 1550 nm photons.

articleTitle: Modifying thermal signatures with the plasmonic phase-change material In3SbTe2
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We employ the plasmonic Phase-Change Material In-SbTe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(IST) for direct laser-writing of functional infrared metasurfaces, without the need for cumbersome cleanroom fabrication. We demonstrate rapid prototyping of large area metasurfaces for controlling thermal emission, beam steering, lensing and also create IR holograms into IST films. This work paves the way towards modifying thermal signatures of objects and fooling infrared cameras on large-scales.

articleTitle: Characterization of Partially Diffuse Objects with Photonic Lanterns
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We study and test photonic lanterns in the context of the profilometry of a stochastic phase object, finding utility in the characterization of partially diffuse targets, whose transmission or reflection profiles can be characterized via spatial mode demultiplexing.

articleTitle: Controlled Concentration of Short DNA Molecules on The Electrodes Using AC Electric Fields and Capillary Flow
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Point-of-care biomarker detection in sessile drops requires minimizing the coffee ring produced by the capillary flow. To address this issue, we have utilized AC electric fields to produce counterflow to capillary flow and slow down the buffer flow and concentrated molecules in the electrodes.

articleTitle: Photonic Lattice Physics: Singular states, Rytov Solutions, and Effect of Defects
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Recently discovered properties of guided-mode resonant photonic lattices are presented. Singular states appearing as isolated spectral lines are modeled accurately by Rytov-type effective medium theory. Inclusion of defects is shown to transit a lattice from a dark state to a bright state resonance.

articleTitle: Occlusion-aided 3D Non-Line-of-Sight Imaging without Time-Resolved Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We demonstrate 3D imaging of a hidden scene from non-time-resolved measurements by opportunistically ex-ploiting a hidden 3D occluder. Using an alternating minimization algorithm, the hidden light-occluder is reconstructed in 3D, while other light-emitting hidden objects that contribute to the measured penumbra are reconstructed in 2D.

articleTitle: Light absorption enhancement in a textured subwavelength mercury cadmium telluride layer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: The absorption enhancement in a textured subwavelength thick Mercury-Cadmium- Telluride layer has been numerically investigated. The absorption is comparable to a non-textured bulk layer facilitating a ~4x reduction in volume. Achieving comparable absorption at a reduced volume has the potential to reduce noise in infrared photodetectors.

articleTitle: Real-Time Hydration Biomarker Monitoring via Optical Sensor Microneedle Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Dehydration poses significant risks to operators, impacting cognitive and physical performance. We developed a wearable monitor using microneedle optical sensing, tracking hydration biomarkers in interstitial fluid. Validation studies showed strong correlations with urine specific gravity, highlighting its potential to mitigate dehydration risks.

articleTitle: Nanomaterials for Ultrafast and Chiral Plasmonics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Ultrafast nonlinear and chiral photonic applications are often limited by the available choice of naturally occurring materials and their generally weak responses. Here, we will discuss novel plasmonic nanomaterials and hetero-nanostructures for tailoring hot-electron dynamics, plasmonic nonlinearities, ultrashort pulse manipulation and chirality.

articleTitle: Hybrid Photonic-Plasmonic Littrow Retroreflectors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: - Using numerical modeling it is shown that performance of Littrow retroreflectors can be enhanced at both polarizations of incident light due to resonantly enhanced plasmonic light scattering in slot arrays formed by Au, Ag, AI, and Cu metallic stripes with 20–40 nm thicknesses.

articleTitle: Periodic Multipolar Arrangement for Photodetector and Tailored Emissivity Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We study multipole Mie resonances in transition metal carbides and nitrides MXene arrays. We also demonstrate how to harness iron pyrite's absorption losses to tailor mid-infrared thermal emitter emissivity through multipole resonance and non-radiative losses.

articleTitle: Higher Harmonic Spectra of Radio Frequency Biomarker Responses Enable Label-free Biosensing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: It is currently difficult to rapidly detect unknown biomarkers. To address this issue, we developed a device for label-free detection using higher harmonic spectra of biomarker responses to low frequency electric fields (<10 kHz).

articleTitle: Flexible Thermochromic Coatings for Thermal Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Thermochromic coatings containing VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> have been proposed for a wide range of thermal management applications from spacecraft radiators to smart windows. To meet these needs, we have developed a technique for transferring VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> films onto on polymers or other lower temperature substrates.

articleTitle: Polarization-Dependent Absorption in GaSb-based Quantum Cascade Detectors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We present a study on the characterization of InAs/AlSb quantum cascade detectors (QCDs) grown strainbalanced on GaSb substrates. The high-quality growth, design, and characterization of strain-compensated structures results in polarization-dependent absorption that is attributed to both intersubband and interband transitions.

articleTitle: Measurement of Raman Gain Coefficients for Liquid-Filled Fiber Multispectral Lasers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Using a referential technique, we measure the Ra-man cross-section, frequency shift, linewidth, and gain coefficients of several solvents at 532 nm and dispersion-correct to 1064 nm. We fill a fiber with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{CBrCl}_{3}$</tex>, characterize its stimulated Raman spectrum, and discuss applicability for multispectral LiDAR.

articleTitle: Sub-nanosecond periodic pulsing via gain switching in a large array of semiconductor blue lasers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We report on direct electrical modulation of a 23-laser array emitting at blue wavelength, resulting in gain-switched pulses. Physical properties of the blue lasers can be extracted from the typical sub-nanosecond pulse width.

articleTitle: Topological Insulator Based Polarization Sensitive Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Polarimetric sensors offer advanced information about an image beyond traditional intensity-based imagers. Topological insulators have inherent properties that allow polarization sensitive detection across a large spectral range without the need for bulky optics. We present a Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-based single pixel detector that demonstrates polarization sensitive photocurrents.

articleTitle: Stimulated Raman Scattering in Oxygen-Filled Fiber for Atmospheric Transmission Optimized LiDAR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We present a multispectral LiDAR source based on stimulated Raman scattering in a pressurized oxygen-filled antiresonant fiber. The 1.064 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu m$</tex> laser, two generated vibrational Stokes orders, and surrounding rotational orders are contained in and spectrally fill the SWIR atmospheric transmission windows.

articleTitle: Fast Optical Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We report a fast optical reconfigurable intelligent surface based on the critically coupled GaAs photonic crystal cavity with graphene and 2D material based dispersive thin-film. The structure was designed to operate at a 1,050 nm wavelength and for high-speed modulation with the use of a TCO material as a lossy layer.

articleTitle: Low-Loss near-UV Light Transmission through Anti-Resonant Hollow-Core Fiber
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We present a low-loss nested anti-resonant hollow-core fiber in the near-UV range. The characterized fiber shows a wide transmission window exceeding 40 nm near 390 nm wavelength with a loss <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< 30$</tex> dB/km. The lowest measured loss is found to be 7.3 dB/km at 402 nm.

articleTitle: Super-Bandwidth Detection using a Real-Time, Gapless Broadband Photonics Spectrogram with High Frequency Resolution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We recover the time-frequency representation of a 21 GHz RF bandwidth signal with 4.48 nanosecond time resolution in real-time without acquisition gaps using a 6 GHz detector. This is enabled by the high frequency resolution of a time-mapped spectrogram based on a Talbot array illuminator.

articleTitle: Infrared Absorption Studies on BSA-Templated Gold Nanocrystals on Silicon Metasurface Supporting Quasi Bound-State-in-Continuum Resonance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Selective enhancement of Infrared absorption of amide-B vibrational mode from Bovine serum albumin templated gold nanocrystals (BSA-Au NCs) utilizing quasi bound-state-in-the-continuum (quasi-BIC) resonance in silicon metasurface is studied. Design, fabrication and experimental characterization of the metasurfaces with and without BSA-Au NCs is presented.

articleTitle: High Gain Low Noise InGaAs Avalanche Photodiode
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We report electro-optical characteristics of an InGaAs APD which can achieve a Gain of 100 with over 8 V of operational dynamic range and compare it with a planar design InGaAs APD. They both exhibit low dark current and low Noise Equivalent Power.

articleTitle: Radiance Field Sampling for Unresolved Specular Object Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We introduce a novel technique for classifying unresolved specular objects. In remote sensing targets of interest like drones, helicopters, planes, cars, or satellites are often under-resolved. If those targets have specular surface characteristics, like metallic bodies or windows for example, there will be “glint” instances in detection which correspond to high signal levels from the specular surface on that target. The radiance field from a specular surface will be distributed spatially in a way that depends on the shape of that surface. And, as the target, source, or imaging system moves, one can collect a time-series sample of that radiance field and use that data to classify the unresolved surface which generated that field. This allows us to extract useful target information even if we are operating in an unresolved and/or turbulent regime, since specular signals provide high-signal information about the surface compared to diffuse surfaces, especially at long ranges. By employing both active and passive illumination schemes we demonstrate this concept in the lab and at a range of 4.7 km.

articleTitle: Using Hybrid Optical-Electronic Neural Network for Demultiplexing Multiplexed Orbital Angular Momentum Beams
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Here, we introduce a hybrid optical-electronic neural network to demultiplex the multiplexed orbital angular momentum (OAM) beams under various atmospheric turbulence conditions. Current results show a demultiplexing accuracy of 71.56% under strong turbulence levels.

articleTitle: Circuit Theory for Anomalies in Light Scattering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We apply the lumped element circuit theory to explore anomalies in light scattering within the complex frequency domain. This approach unveils insights into phenomena like virtual absorption, bound states in the continuum, critical coupling, and advancing photonics by enabling sophisticated design and analysis of optical systems.

articleTitle: Dual-Stacked Photonic Crystal for Transmissive Filtering Fabricated by Two- Photon Polymerization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: The combination of two periodic dielectric stacks is presented as an alternative to introducing defect layers for inducing a narrow transmissive region within the reflective photonic bandgap. This method increases the overall bandgap width when compared with a single periodic stack with a defect. While the transmissive band is not as narrow as in the defect design, the transmission region does demonstrate less sensitivity to layer thickness non-uniformity. The dual-stacked photonic crystal may be more compatible with fabrication by two-photon polymerization for inducing a transmission band within the photonic bandgap.

articleTitle: An Equivalent Currents Approach to Generating Simulated Training Data for RF Image Classifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Robust classification of RF images via machine learning approaches typically requires significant amounts of training data. Training with synthetic data is of interest in order to achieve sufficient samples for arbitrary scenarios of interest. However, generating high-fidelity target models for use in simulation can require significant manual effort and time. To mitigate this challenge, we present a new strategy for generating target scattering models directly from RF measurements based on the principle of equivalent currents.

articleTitle: A Scientific Approach for Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: The All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) is applying a scientific approach coordinated with defense, intelligence, academic, and industry partners in identifying and understanding Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) through application of technology to detect, identify, and characterize UAP operating in the vicinity of sensitive air spaces.

articleTitle: Ge-on-Si APD with Diagonal Dual Injection in 45nm SOl SiPh Process
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: A small form factor high gain Ge-on-Si APD is demonstrated in 45nm silicon photonic technology. The design utilizes dual optical injection to germanium absorption region using a pair of waveguide tapers. For 1550 nm wavelength the device achieves ~14 A/A gain at 3.5V reverse bias

articleTitle: Epsilon-Near-Zero Photonics in Planar and Optical Fiber Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: In this talk, I will discuss our recent studies on tunable linear and nonlinear optical properties of conducting oxide and metallic nitride epsilon-near-zero materials in planar and optical fiber platforms.

articleTitle: Exploring curved metasurface optics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We explore the advantages of creating a meta-surface optical element on a curved rather than planar surface. Extension of the recent notions of meta-surface dispersion engineering to curved surfaces is a daunting challenge, but our analysis shows curved meta-surfaces potentially represent a fruitful research direction for high-performance optical systems.

articleTitle: Nonlocal Dielectric Metalens for Long-Wavelength Infrared Imging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We propose and experimentally demonstrate a wavelength-selective nonlocal metasurface lens for long-wave infrared wavelengths based on quasi-bound states in the continuum. The dielectric metalens fabrication and its experimental characterization using custom-built infrared microscope are discussed in details.

articleTitle: Gain-shaped terahertz quantum cascade laser frequency combs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We demonstrate that adding carefully engineered resonant loss to a quantum cascade laser cavity can counteract the diffusive effect of the gain medium, allowing broader bandwidth combs to form. An improvement of 30\% in comb bandwidth is reported.

articleTitle: THz-Frequency Free-Standing Bi-Layer wire grid Polarizers Fabricated by Stereolithography
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Finite element simulations of free-standing, bi-layer wire grid polarizers, with dimensions typical for stereo-lithography, show two orders of magnitude improvement over single-layer wire grid polarizers.

articleTitle: Compact Photonic Microwave System for RADAR and EW Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We present an ultra-stable photonic microwave system generating carrier signals from the L- to K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</inf>-bands. From these sources tunable frequencies across the X-band are synthesized. The system is conceived to be realized within a single 4HU standard 19-inch rack form factor, featuring full automated operation. (Abstract)

articleTitle: Exploring AlGaInP for Use in Si Photomultiplier Analogs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We present a materials study of AlGaInP grown on GaAs leveraging deep-level optical spectroscopy and time resolved photoluminescence. Our materials may serve as the basis for wide-bandgap analogs of silicon photomultipliers optimized for short wavelength sensing.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Leaky Wave Antenna Design for K-Band and W-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: A bi-directional dual-band meta-surface antenna designed to operate at 20 GHz in the longitudinal direction and 80 GHz in the transverse direction is described and simulation results are presented.
